restated: Let f(q,r) be defined by the Brouwer recurrence (MISSION section 2), B_c(x)=f(c+x,c)-(c+x) when f(c+x,c)>=c+x (undefined otherwise). For each row c let p_c be its eventual period (p_c=1 if row c has only finitely many P-positions [p,q,c] with p>=q) and N(c) its preperiod as in MISSION, with N(c) = 1 + the last such q for a row with finitely many. For r>=1 let q_r = lcm{p_c : c<r}, sigma_r = max_{c<r} N(c) - r, and V''(a) = union over c<r of {B_c(a+r-c)} (defined values only). Then a -> V''(a) is q_r-periodic for all a >= max(sigma_r,0). This lemma claims no bound on any N(c).
ledger_statement: DETERMINISM ONSET (structural; no bound claimed). For every r>=1, V''(a) is q_r-periodic for all a >= max(sigma_r,0), sigma_r := max_{c<r} N(c) - r, where for a stale row N(c) is 1 + the last q with a P-position [p,q,c], p>=q. Proof componentwise: V''_{r,c}(a)=B_c(a+r-c) is evaluated at x>=u_c=N(c)-c iff a>=N(c)-r, where B_c is p_c-periodic (live c) or undefined (stale c). Hence the merged-trail machine is autonomous from a=max(sigma_r,0). sigma_r is expressed through the N(c), c<r; the lemma does not bound them.

verdicts.gap_description: No non-following step found in either lemma; I verified both line by line and computationally. Only a notational nit: at r = 1 the claim's sigma_r = max_{c<r} N(c) - r and q_r = lcm{p_c : c<r} are max/lcm over the empty set; with the standard conventions (sigma_1 = -infinity, q_1 = 1) the statement is true there since V'' is identically empty. Worth one line of convention, not a gap.

verdicts.gap_description: (FR) is asserted as an exact reformulation of the MISSION section 2 recurrence (or of 'Zeilberger's Fundamental Recurrence') but is never derived from section 2, and no precise citation is given for the named recurrence. The equivalence is not formal: section 2 uses mex over positive integers, (FR) uses mex over non-negative integers, and the identification holds exactly because f(q,r) >= q at every step the machine runs (copy-rule argument for live rows; C0029 for the stale-row endpoint). I verified the identity computationally (41,344 direct tests, ~451k machine steps, 0 failures), so the gap is fillable by a short derivation, but the written proof omits it. Two minor secondary gaps: (i) the invariant 'H_{a+1} = dec(H_a) u {k_a - 1} subset [0, m_r - 1]' is literally false at the terminating step (k_a = 0 gives {-1}), rescued only by the termination convention; (ii) 'm_r <= r + 1' invokes '#G07 section 8.1' which is not in the declared dependency list (verified numerically: f(q,c) <= q+c+1 with worst slack 0 on q,r <= 260).

verdicts.effectivity_check: No computable bound is produced, and the submission says so explicitly: 'sigma_r is defined through the preperiods N(c), c < r. The lemma says when the machine becomes autonomous, given those preperiods. It does not bound them, and it does not bound N(r). It becomes effective exactly to the extent that a computable bound on N(c) is supplied from elsewhere.' There is no line producing an evaluable constant: sigma_r = max_{c<r} N(c) - r references the N(c), whose existence is Byrnes' non-effective theorem. So the lemma alone does not make Byrnes effective and would not give a bound evaluable at r = 1000; but it does not claim to, so this is not the circularity trap — merely a (correct) structural lemma whose effectivity must come from elsewhere (the cited C0029 supplies it only for stale rows).
